ko_meaning: 나를 낳아 준 여자 부모를 부르는 말
ko_meaning_en: A word for the female parent who gave birth to you

form.q_en: Pick the particle that makes 'mom' the subject.
form.why: 가 marks the subject after a vowel. 를/을 mark an object, and 에 means 'at/to'.

ko_meaning_en: A friendly word for your father

form.q_en: Pick the word that means 'and' (Dad and Mom are at home).
form.why: 하고 joins two nouns: 'dad and mom'. 을 marks an object, 에 a place, and 이 is used only after a consonant.

ko_meaning: 쌀로 만든 음식. 또는 아침, 점심, 저녁에 먹는 음식
ko_meaning_en: Food made from rice; also the food you eat at breakfast, lunch, or dinner

tokens.note: 을 marks the object (after a consonant)
밥을 하다 = to cook rice; 하 + 여요 → 해요

form.q_en: Pick the object particle for 밥.
form.why: 밥 ends in a consonant (ㅂ), so it takes 을. 를 is for words ending in a vowel.

ko_meaning_en: The thing that shines brightly in the sky during the day

example.en: I saw the sun in the morning.

form.q_en: Pick the particle that makes 'the sun' the object.
form.why: 해 ends in a vowel, so the object particle is 를. 가 would make the sun the one who saw.

ko_meaning_en: The round thing that shines in the sky at night

example.en: The moon is pretty at night.

tokens.note: 이 marks the subject (after a consonant)

form.q_en: Pick the subject particle for 달.
form.why: 달 ends in a consonant (ㄹ), so the subject particle is 이. 을/를 mark objects, and 예쁘다 has no object.

ko_meaning_en: A greeting you say when you meet someone

form.q_en: Complete the polite greeting.
form.why: The greeting is the fixed phrase 안녕하세요, with the respectful ending -세요.

ko_meaning_en: What you say when you are thankful

form.q_en: Complete the formal 'thank you'.
form.why: The formal ending -ㅂ니다 joins 하 as 합니다, so the phrase is 감사합니다.

ko_meaning_en: What you say to answer that something is right

form.q_en: Answer 'yes' to the question.
form.why: B says 좋아해요 ('I like it'), so the answer starts with 네 'yes'. 아니요 would contradict it.

ko_meaning_en: What you say to answer that something is not so

tokens.note: 안 before a verb or adjective makes it negative

form.q_en: Make the sentence negative: 'No, I'm not hungry.'
form.why: 안 goes right before a verb or adjective to say 'not'. 도, 는 and 을 are particles and must follow a noun.

ko_meaning_en: To have no problem; to be fine

tokens.note: present tense, polite (-아요); ㅎ is silent

form.q_en: Pick the correct polite ending.
form.why: The last vowel of 괜찮 is ㅏ, so it takes -아요: 괜찮아요. 괜찮어요 is a common spelling mistake.

ko_meaning_en: The word the speaker uses for himself or herself

tokens.note: 도 means 'too, also'; 나 is casual, 저 is the polite 'I'

form.q_en: Pick the subject form of 나.
form.why: With the subject particle 가, 나 changes to 내: 내가. 나가 is not used.

ko_meaning_en: A person you are close to

example.en: I want to meet my friend.

form.q_en: Pick the particle for the person you meet.
form.why: 친구 ends in a vowel, so it takes 를. 을 is for words ending in a consonant.

ko_meaning: 남자, 여자, 아이를 모두 이르는 말
ko_meaning_en: A word for any man, woman, or child

example.en: There are many people in the park.

tokens.note: 이 marks the subject (after a consonant)

form.q_en: Pick the subject particle for 사람.
form.why: 사람 ends in a consonant (ㅁ), so the subject particle is 이. 가 is for words ending in a vowel.

ko_meaning: 엄마, 아빠, 아이처럼 같이 사는 사람들
ko_meaning_en: People who live together, like mom, dad, and children

example.en: I looked at a family photo.

tokens.note: a noun can describe the next noun: 'family photo'

form.q_en: Pick the word for 'with' (I live together with my family).
form.why: 하고 means 'with'. 와 is used only after a vowel; after 족 it would be 과.

ko_meaning_en: A young person

form.q_en: Pick the subject particle for 아이.
form.why: 아이 ends in a vowel, so the subject particle is 가. 이 is for words ending in a consonant.

ko_meaning: 여자가 나이가 많은 여자 형제를 부르는 말
ko_meaning_en: A word a woman or girl uses for her older sister

example.en: My older sister is an office worker.

form.q_en: Say 'It's my older sister's bag.'
form.why: 의 shows belonging, like 's in English: 언니의 가방 'sister's bag'.

ko_meaning: 여자가 나이가 많은 남자 형제를 부르는 말
ko_meaning_en: A word a woman or girl uses for her older brother

form.q_en: A girl talks about her older brother. Pick the right word.
form.why: A girl calls her older brother 오빠. A boy would say 형, and 누나/언니 mean older sister.

ko_meaning_en: A brother or sister younger than you

tokens.note: 이 marks the subject (after a consonant)

form.q_en: Pick the subject particle for 동생.
form.why: 동생 ends in a consonant (ㅇ), so the subject particle is 이.

ko_meaning: 남자가 나이가 많은 남자 형제를 부르는 말
ko_meaning_en: A word a man or boy uses for his older brother

example.en: I watched a movie with my older brother.

form.q_en: Pick the word for 'with' that fits after 형.
form.why: 형 ends in a consonant (ㅇ), so 'with' is 과. 와 is used after a vowel.

ko_meaning: 남자가 나이가 많은 여자 형제를 부르는 말
ko_meaning_en: A word a man or boy uses for his older sister

example.en: My older sister gave me a gift.

form.q_en: A boy talks about his older sister. Pick the right word.
form.why: A boy calls his older sister 누나. A girl would say 언니, and 오빠/형 mean older brother.

ko_meaning_en: The mother of your dad or mom

tokens.note: -세요 shows respect to an older person

form.q_en: Pick the respectful form for Grandma.
form.why: Speaking about an older person, add -세요 to show respect: 가세요. 가다 is only the dictionary form.

ko_meaning_en: The father of your dad or mom

tokens.note: -세요 shows respect to an older person

form.q_en: Pick the topic particle for 할아버지.
form.why: 할아버지 ends in a vowel, so the topic particle is 는. 은 is for words ending in a consonant.

ko_meaning: 태어난 지 얼마 안 된 아주 어린 아이
ko_meaning_en: A very young child who was born not long ago

form.q_en: Yesterday the baby slept a lot. Pick the right verb form.
form.why: 어제 'yesterday' needs the past tense: 자 + 았어요 → 잤어요.

ko_meaning_en: A person who is not a woman, like a dad or an older brother

form.q_en: Pick the word for 'and' that fits after 남자.
form.why: 남자 ends in a vowel, so 'and' is 와. 과 is used after a consonant.

ko_meaning_en: A person who is not a man, like a mom or an older sister

tokens.note: 그 points to someone already mentioned

form.q_en: Pick the topic particle for 여자.
form.why: 여자 ends in a vowel, so the topic particle is 는. 은 is for words ending in a consonant.

ko_meaning_en: The clear, colorless thing people drink

example.en: I drank a lot of water.

tokens.note: 을 marks the object (after a consonant)

form.q_en: Ask for water: pick the right particle.
form.why: 물 ends in a consonant (ㄹ), so the object particle is 을. 를 is for words ending in a vowel.

ko_meaning_en: Food made from flour and baked

example.en: I have bread and milk in the morning.

form.q_en: Pick the word for 'and' that fits after 빵.
form.why: 빵 ends in a consonant (ㅇ), so 'and' is 과. 와 is used after a vowel.

ko_meaning: 배추 같은 채소로 만든 매운 한국 음식
ko_meaning_en: A spicy Korean food made from vegetables like cabbage

form.q_en: Pick the object particle for 김치.
form.why: 김치 ends in a vowel, so the object particle is 를. 을 is for words ending in a consonant.

ko_meaning_en: The white drink that comes from cows

form.q_en: Pick the object particle for 우유.
form.why: 우유 ends in a vowel, so the object particle is 를. 을 is for words ending in a consonant.

ko_meaning_en: The flesh of animals like cows and pigs, eaten as food

form.q_en: Pick the subject particle for 고기.
form.why: 고기 ends in a vowel, so the subject particle is 가. 맛있다 describes the subject, so 를 does not fit.

ko_meaning: 음식을 입에 넣어 배 속으로 보내다
ko_meaning_en: To put food in your mouth and send it to your stomach

form.q_en: Yesterday my sibling ate ramen. Pick the right verb form.
form.why: 어제 'yesterday' needs the past tense: 먹 + 었어요 → 먹었어요. -으세요 is for respected people, not a younger sibling.

ko_meaning: 물이나 우유 같은 것을 입으로 넘기다
ko_meaning_en: To swallow something like water or milk

form.q_en: Say 'I want to drink coffee.'
form.why: 'Want to' is verb stem + -고 싶어요: 마시 + 고 싶어요.

ko_meaning_en: For food to taste good

tokens.note: a noun can describe the next noun

form.q_en: Pick the correct polite form of 맛있다.
form.why: The last vowel of 맛있 is ㅣ, so it takes -어요: 맛있어요.

ko_meaning_en: To have an empty stomach and want to eat

form.q_en: Pick the correct polite form of 배고프다.
form.why: ㅡ drops before -아/어요. The vowel before it is ㅗ, so it becomes 배고파요.

ko_meaning: 무엇이 좋아서 자주 하고 싶거나 갖고 싶다
ko_meaning_en: To find something good and want to have it or do it often

form.q_en: 좋아하다 takes an object. Pick the right particle.
form.why: 좋아하다 takes an object, and 생선 ends in a consonant, so it is 을. (좋다 would take 이: 생선이 좋아요.)

ko_meaning_en: The small things that twinkle in the night sky

example.en: There are many stars in the sky.

form.q_en: Pick the subject particle for 별.
form.why: 별 ends in a consonant (ㄹ), so the subject particle is 이. 가 is for words ending in a vowel.

ko_meaning: 머리 위로 높고 넓게 보이는 곳
ko_meaning_en: The high, wide space you see above your head

example.en: A bird flies in the sky.

tokens.note: 을 can mark the space you move through

form.q_en: Pick the particle for the space the bird flies through.
form.why: With 날다, the space you move through takes 을/를. 하늘 ends in a consonant, so it is 을.

ko_meaning_en: Water that falls from the sky

tokens.note: 비가 오다 = it rains; 오 + 았어요 → 왔어요

form.q_en: Yesterday it rained a lot. Pick the right verb form.
form.why: 어제 'yesterday' needs the past tense: 오 + 았어요 → 왔어요. Rain 'comes' in Korean: 비가 와요.

ko_meaning_en: Moving air

form.q_en: Pick the subject particle for 바람.
form.why: 바람 ends in a consonant (ㅁ), so the subject particle is 이. The wind is the one blowing, so 을/를 do not fit.

ko_meaning_en: The pretty thing that blooms on trees and plants

tokens.note: ㅊ is sounded before a vowel: [꼬츨]

form.q_en: Pick the object particle for 꽃.
form.why: 꽃 ends in a consonant (ㅊ), so the object particle is 을. 를 is for words ending in a vowel.

ko_meaning_en: A place where the land rises very high

example.en: I go to the mountains on the weekend.

form.q_en: Pick the particle for where you go.
form.why: With 가다, the place you go to takes 에. 에서 marks where an action happens.

ko_meaning: 아주 넓고 짠 물이 있는 곳
ko_meaning_en: A very wide place of salty water

example.en: I had fun at the sea in the summer.

tokens.note: 에서 marks where an action happens

form.q_en: Pick the particle for where you played.
form.why: 놀다 is an action, so the place takes 에서. 에 is for where something is or where you go.

ko_meaning_en: A place where water flows a long way

example.en: There are many fish in the river.

form.q_en: Pick the particle for where the fish are.
form.why: 에 marks the place where something is: 강에 'in the river'.

ko_meaning_en: A plant that grows tall from the ground

tokens.note: noun + 아래 = under the noun; 에서 marks where you do something

form.q_en: Pick the subject particle for 나무.
form.why: 나무 ends in a vowel, so the subject particle is 가. 이 is for words ending in a consonant.

ko_meaning_en: An animal that lives and swims in water

tokens.note: 에서 marks where you do something

form.q_en: Pick the word for living fish in the sea.
form.why: 물고기 is a living fish. 생선 is fish as food, at the market or on the table.

ko_meaning_en: The part of the face you see with

tokens.note: 의 ('s) is often dropped in speech

form.q_en: Say 'the baby's eyes'.
form.why: 의 shows belonging, like 's: 아기의 눈 'the baby's eyes'.

ko_meaning_en: The part of the face you smell with

tokens.note: 가 marks the subject: 'as for Dad, the nose is big'

form.q_en: Pick the subject particle for 코.
form.why: 코 ends in a vowel, so the subject particle is 가. 이 is for words ending in a consonant.

ko_meaning_en: The part of the face you eat and talk with

example.en: There is rice in your mouth.

form.q_en: Pick the particle for where the rice is.
form.why: With 있다, the place where something is takes 에. 에서 is for where an action happens.

ko_meaning_en: The part on the side of the head you hear with

tokens.note: 의 ('s) is often dropped in speech

form.q_en: Pick the subject particle for 귀.
form.why: 귀 ends in a vowel, so the subject particle is 가. 이 is for words ending in a consonant.

ko_meaning: 팔 끝에 있어서 물건을 잡는 곳
ko_meaning_en: The part at the end of the arm that holds things

tokens.note: -으세요 after a consonant makes a polite request

form.q_en: Pick the object particle for 손.
form.why: 손 ends in a consonant (ㄴ), so the object particle is 을. 를 is for words ending in a vowel.
